desks.Dividends: Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter (pay Dec 10), is the only declared watchlist ex-date in the window, its 24th consecutive annual increase on the Sep 15 raise from $0.91. Apple's Q4 dividend is still undeclared: a Nov 10 listing from one source is a projection, UNVERIFIED as a declaration, with declaration watch on the Nov 2 earnings print. Nvidia's next dividend is undeclared, SPY and QQQ point to December on pattern only, Tesla pays no dividend, and no cuts or specials were found.
desks.Earnings: Microsoft reported FY27 Q1 after the close Wed Oct 28: revenue $92.3 billion (+19%), non-GAAP EPS $4.89 (+18%) vs $4.71 Nasdaq consensus, Azure +48%, Microsoft Cloud $63.9 billion (+30%), read from the release itself. Guidance from the 5:30 p.m. ET call was not confirmed in this package. Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close (call 5:00 p.m. ET) with an implied move of about 4.0-4.4%. Nvidia's Nov 18 date is outside the window; Tesla reported Oct 21.
desks.Futures: EIA (week ended Oct 23, released today): crude -1.9 million barrels to 410.6 million vs a +15K-barrel poll expectation, distillates -1.5 million barrels and about 10% below the five-year average, gasoline +3.9 million barrels. Kpler disputes EIA's export figure (about 1 million barrels per day lower on observed loadings), so the export-driven draw carries a discount. The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% (10-2); NAVCENT advised vessels to remain well clear of Hormuz today. Next catalysts: Core PCE and Q3 GDP Thu Oct 29 at 8:30 a.m. ET, EIA gas Thu, OPEC+ meeting and Iran's Sinokor deadline Sun Nov 1. Yahoo's Brent Oct 28 close ($110.43) contradicts news prints and is NOT used as a settlement fact.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found this week. The one feed item: Cboe's new BOX20X26 box-rate index value for the Nov 20 SPX option series begins disseminating from Nov 20, a feed addition, not a methodology change. A Saxo options brief derives its SPX ranges from put-call parity as a pricing anchor and reports no deviation.
desks.Premium: Close marks, not live quotes (pull ran 13:29-13:31 PT, after the 16:00 ET options close). SPY 11.6% vs 10.05% realized is roughly fairly priced; QQQ is WINDOW-CONTINGENT (one day drives 30.67% of its 20-day realized window), so no clean verdict is issued for it. Apple Oct 30 at 19.8% is 1.47x realized with no event inside that expiry, but its quotes were crossed post-close, so 19.8% is approximate; the Nov 4 expiry at 34.8% holds the earnings hump. Microsoft's event has passed: Oct 30 straddle $26.75 = 5.04% move, pre-release marks now stale. Nvidia 35.7% vs 31.05% realized is mildly rich; Tesla 35.5% vs 37.76% sits below realized. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names.
desks.Quant lab: Two new candidates were scored and appended to the ledger (#168-169), both ARCHIVE: an American-option operator-splitting paper (score 31) and a Hawkes-process order-placement paper (score 34), neither with author code linked and neither a desk procedure. No TEST or INTEGRATE movement this run. The GitHub new-repo discovery leg failed transient (empty replies twice) and the Semantic Scholar leg 429'd twice, so new-repo coverage is NOT complete today and the search leg must be retried tomorrow.

headline: Daily research brief — Wednesday, October 28

items.detail: The Fed held the target range at 3.75%-4.00% on a 10-2 vote, with dissenters Cook and Hammack preferring a 25-basis-point hike now, upgraded growth language to a strong pace, and kept December live. Microsoft reported FY27 Q1 after the close: revenue $92.3 billion (+19%), non-GAAP EPS $4.89 (+18%) against a $4.71 Nasdaq consensus, Azure +48%, Microsoft Cloud $63.9 billion (+30%). Thursday is the first full reaction session for both. Guidance from Microsoft's 5:30 p.m. ET call was not confirmed in this package, and Thursday at 8:30 a.m. ET brings Core PCE and Q3 GDP.
items.title: Fed holds, Microsoft beats — Thursday is the first full reaction session

items.detail: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close, with an options-implied move of about 4.0-4.4% (Nov 4 and Nov 6 straddles) against a recent realized earnings-day average of 2.9% mean and 1.9% median over the last four quarters. The Nov 4 expiry shows the textbook earnings hump: implied volatility 19.8% for Oct 30 rising to 34.8% for Nov 4, a 15-point jump. Premium into Nov 2 carries event risk plus post-print implied-volatility crush. The nearer Oct 30 expiry is separately rich at 1.47x realized with no event inside it, but its quotes were crossed post-close, so treat 19.8% as approximate.
items.title: Apple on Nov 2 is the live avoid

items.detail: Pre-decision FRED prints dated Oct 27 put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.70%, and the 10-year at 4.99%, a 2s10s spread of +29 basis points, down from +41 on Aug 31 as the 2-year rose faster than the 10-year. SOFR sits 7 basis points over the effective fed funds rate: orderly funding, no stress signal. Post-decision market prints moved higher instead: 2-year 4.776%, 10-year 5.047%. The first post-decision FRED read arrives Oct 29. Higher-for-longer keeps discount-rate pressure on long-duration growth multiples.
items.title: Rates rose after the hold; funding stays calm

items.detail: EIA (week ended Oct 23, released today 10:30 a.m. ET): crude drew 1.9 million barrels to 410.6 million against a poll expectation of a small build, and distillates fell 1.5 million barrels to about 10% below the five-year average, while gasoline built 3.9 million barrels. Ship-tracker Kpler disputes EIA's export figure, about 1 million barrels per day lower on observed loadings, so the export-driven draw should be discounted. US Naval Forces Central Command advised vessels today to remain well clear of Hormuz, and Houthis claimed an Oct 27 strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (550K barrels per day). The next binaries are the Nov 1 OPEC+ meeting and Iran's Nov 1 Sinokor-tanker enforcement deadline.
items.title: Energy: a draw surprise plus a live Hormuz premium
